newsitem.title: KENYA: Rwandan court acquits genocide suspect, radio says.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan court acquits genocide suspect, radio says.

text.p: A court in central Rwanda has acquitted a defendant charged with genocide and crimes against humanity, the second suspect to be acquitted since trials began in December.
State radio said on Thursday a court in Nyamata town acquitted Joseph Karega on Wednesay as it proved "beyond doubt he was not guilty of the crimes of genocide and other crimes against humanity".
The radio, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, said Karega was the second person to be acquitted.
At least 18 people have been sentenced to death in Rwanda since December for involvement in the 1994 genocide of 800,000 Tutsis and Hutu moderates by Hutu troops, militiamen and mobs.
Some 100,000 people accused of involvement in the mass slaughter three years ago are still held in jails and lock-ups.
The London-based human rights group Amnesty International said on Tuesday most genocide trials in Rwanda were unfair with many defendants presumed to be guilty unless they were proved innocent.
